claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page linked from the support index).
The Pulumi Provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi's provider support policy designates certain providers as receiving long-term security updates, while other providers do not.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending operations in progress, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`; it compares the desired state in the program against the last recorded state.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.

Pulumi auto-naming creates each resource's physical name by combining the logical name with a random suffix, which also lets Pulumi replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old resource.
Auto-naming can be disabled per-resource, and via project or stack configuration can be customized or disabled globally, per provider, or per resource type.
During an update, Pulumi secrets are decrypted in memory and visible to the Pulumi program.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key for every stack, used to encrypt secrets for that stack, and this is configurable to use a custom secrets provider.

Passing `--secret` to `pulumi config set` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`; encrypting the same value across two stacks yields different encrypted strings, so encrypted values cannot be copied between files with a text editor.
When running a preview, update or destroy, Pulumi decrypts secret config data, which is plain text during execution and accessible to any part of the program via the config object.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way, but some Pulumi providers use open-source Terraform schemas to determine available resources, parameters and attributes.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi is a declarative tool that uses imperative languages to define the end state; the language is used for authoring the program, not for talking to the cloud provider API.
Pulumi uses strongly typed languages that support IntelliSense and the Language Server Protocol, so users rarely need to leave their IDE.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled explicitly with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Pulumi experimental features can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle and are not necessarily supported.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older provider major versions (beyond the latest and the LTS-covered previous major) receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The npm tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi recommends planning a provider update when a major version is released, updating to the latest minor at least quarterly, always allowing patch updates, and never being 2 major versions behind.
Pages exist at /docs/support/faq/secrets-config/, /docs/support/faq/pulumi-cloud/, and /docs/support/faq/policies/.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Pulumi Registry has package pages at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch includes fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship the security patches.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a covered provider ships, it becomes the new N and the old N becomes the new LTS major; the old LTS major reaches end of life on the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major of a covered provider, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is the recommended approach.
For covered providers, older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is the newest release then v3 is N, v2 is N−1 (LTS), and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a Pulumi provider is supported until N+1 ships and receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.
The LTS version (N−1) of a covered provider is supported up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships, and receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
Provider versions N−2 and older are end of life, not supported, and receive no updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'What are the best practices for maintaining provider versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
